summary: Tenant I/O coupling causing gradual capacity bleed and autoscaler unresponsiveness
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (Acme Retail) reports a gradual degradation in dedicated pool throughput during peak window that started ~2026-03-09 11:40 UTC and persisted for multiple hours. The degradation shows as a progressive fall in served tokens/sec and increased queueing despite apparent free GPU slots. Autoscaler did not scale up or rebalance for the affected shard for >18 minutes once p99 latency crossed the SLO.

Impact:
- Production API p50/p95 showed ~30% throughput loss for Acme's dedicated pool (customer-facing).
- Multiple requests were returned with 429s from route fallback logic when the system attempted to fall back to shared capacity.
- Customer-facing latency regressions caused degraded UX for product feature launched that morning.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: pool-id dp-usw-23 (Acme-reserved)
- Region: us-west-2
- Models: redwood-v2-7b (pinned), fallback: gpt-neo-instruct-3.5
- Platform: production, autoscaler enabled with predictive window and cooldown configured

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start a steady burst of short inference streams (50–200 tokens) with high connection churn and frequent small attachments (customer's pattern).
2) Observe allocator logs and pool metrics during sustained start-of-minute flares.
3) Note that kv-prefetch IO increases on the scheduled shard followed by a drop in batch formation efficiency.

Observed behavior:
- GPU slots show as available in allocator state but batcher throughput stalls (p50 token generation drops).
- Autoscaler telemetry indicates belief that capacity is sufficient (no scale up event) while per-GPU IO (nvme read queues) and host CPU sys time increase.
- Prefetch subsystem shows erratic lease renewals; slot attach latency for new sessions climbs from ~60ms to 900ms.

Expected behavior:
- Batch formation remains efficient for short streams and autoscaler should add capacity or trigger rebalance when p99 latency crosses configured SLOs.

Logs / metrics / artifacts:
- Customer metrics (Acme dashboard): https://dashboards.redwood/acme/throughput/2026-03-09
- Allocator trace (shard dp-usw-23): https://logs.redwood/allocator/trace/2026-03-09-11
- Autoscaler event stream: https://logs.redwood/autoscaler/events/2026-03-09
- Kernel-level nvme/io-wait graphs: https://metrics.redwood/host/io-wait/dp-usw-23

Initial hypotheses:
- Cross-tenant I/O coupling: a tenant in the same host group is generating small, high-fanout writes that increase NVMe contention and postpone context switch for the serving process, reducing batch throughput.
- Prefetch/kv-cache lease churn causing slot reservation inconsistency: batcher sees slots as free but attach pipeline is delayed by prefetch backlog.
- Autoscaler configuration (smoothing window/cooldown) is too conservative for this workload pattern, so it fails to react to short-lived but sustained p99 regressions.

Immediate customer-facing workaround requested:
- Temporary increase of burst capacity for Acme's pool and enable aggressive fallback to warm shared instances for the next 2 hours while investigation continues.

Work items for follow-up:
- SRE to collect host-level IO stack traces and perf events for the impacted hosts.
- Scheduler/allocator team to correlate attach latency with nvme IO spikes and identify tenant causing heavy small writes.
- Autoscaler team to evaluate a shorter predictive window for dedicated pools flagged as latency-sensitive.

Priority: P1 (customer-facing degradation).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-10 13:02 - Liam O'Connor (Support): Confirmed customer telemetry and reproduced a scaled-down load pattern in staging; observed same attach latency spikes when background small-file writer process is enabled on host image.

2026-03-10 14:20 - Priya Patel (SRE): Collected perf and iostat during a controlled repro. Found NVMe queue utilization spikes coincident with a high number of tiny synchronous writes (4–8KB) from a background snapshot job running on a co-located tenant. Host CPU sys% rose to 42% and irq/softirq counts increased.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Diego Alvarez (Allocator): Allocator state showed orphaned slot handles being GC'd slowly; attach requests were queued in scheduler due to backpressure on prefetch worker threads. Batcher's batch fill rate dropped ~28%.

2026-03-11 11:00 - Autoscaler team: The predictive model uses 5-minute smoothing with a 10-minute cooldown which allowed the p99 window to persist without triggering scale. Simulated faster window (1m) did trigger scale-ups but caused oscillation in unrelated pools.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:58 - Liam O'Connor (Support): Customer reported initial hit — collecting request IDs and sample payloads. Asked engineering to triage host-level metrics. (sla_first_response: 2026-03-10)
2026-03-10 13:30 - Priya Patel (SRE): Found a correlated host-level IO pattern. Running perf sampling now. Marking this as a candidate noisy-tenant IO coupling issue.
2026-03-10 15:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Notified Acme that we will temporarily increase burst reservation and apply warm shared fallback. Customer approved the temporary change.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Diego Alvarez (Allocator): Deployed a canary allocator patch that tightens prefetch worker backlog limits on two affected hosts. Observed 12% improvement in batch fill rate during test window.

2026-03-11 12:20 - Priya Patel (SRE): Identified suspect tenant (internal id tenant-93) performing frequent small snapshot writes. Opened INT ticket to reach out to owner and schedule staggered snapshot windows. Linked INT-330 for internal coordination.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer confirmed UX improvement after temporary bump; still monitoring. Asking for a timeline for a long-term mitigation.
resolution:
Workaround applied: temporary burst reservation increase for Acme and warm shared fallback enabled for 3 hours (2026-03-10 15:20 to 2026-03-10 18:20). Canary allocator tweak deployed to limit prefetch backlog on affected hosts. Internal tenant (tenant-93) agreed to stagger snapshot jobs — INT coordination ticket created.

Planned permanent fixes:
- Autoscaler tuning: evaluate lowering predictive smoothing for latency-sensitive dedicated pools and add guardrails to avoid oscillation (task created for autoscaler team).
- Prefetch subsystem: add stronger visibility and backpressure metrics; implement faster orphan-handle GC and earlier attach-failure detection.
- Placement policy: better IO-affinity packing rules to avoid co-locating small-write-heavy tenants with low-latency dedicated pools.

Status: In Progress (deployments for autoscaler config and allocator GC improvements scheduled in next sprint).
next_steps:
1) Autoscaler team to run A/B with 1m predictive window for a subset of dedicated pools and monitor oscillation risk (owner: Priya Patel).
2) Scheduler/allocator to produce a host placement advisory and a flag to avoid snapshot-heavy tenants co-located with latency-sensitive pools (owner: Diego Alvarez).
3) CS to follow up with Acme on 2026-03-13 for final verification and close the incident once proof-of-fix deployed.
4) Postmortem and runbook updates to be authored after fixes (owner: Maya Chen).
